title: Deployment Sweep: Controlled Experiments SDK with Adaptive Rollback
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Deliver an API and SDK surface that lets teams safely run canary rollouts, A/B experiments, and shadow traffic with deterministic idempotency and role-based controls, plus an adaptive auto-rollback rule set that integrates with Redwood Console signals. This ticket captures the PM-level requirements, success criteria, proposed endpoint shapes, SDK helper ergonomics, permission model, and testing plan for the first implementation iteration.

Why: Customers require predictable, auditable rollouts that reduce regression risk while keeping operational burden low. Existing primitives are scattered across orchestration and runtime teams; we need a coherent set of client helpers and server contracts so Developers and Platform teams can adopt progressive delivery without building ad hoc tooling.

Scope (iteration 1):
- Server endpoints for creating/updating rollouts, adjusting traffic splits, enabling shadow routes, and triggering/observing auto-rollback state.
- SDK helpers (TypeScript + Python) for createRollout(), updateTraffic(), observeHealth(), reconcile() with idempotency-key support.
- Permission scopes and audit metadata for all mutating actions.
- Basic adaptive rollback rules: threshold on latency/error-rate/n-gram quality regression with cooldown + automatic abort.
- Integration hooks to Console for observability and manual override.

Out of scope (this iteration):
- Full multi-tenant policy engine for cross-org role mapping.
- Complex statistical analysis for long-running A/B (will add in a follow-up).
proposed_endpoints: POST /api/v1/rollouts - create rollout with strategy:{canary|ab|shadow}, targetModel, baselineModel, initialTrafficSplit, idempotency_key
PATCH /api/v1/rollouts/{id}/traffic - atomic update to traffic weights (requires rollout:update scope)
POST /api/v1/rollouts/{id}/shadow - enable/disable shadowing and sampling rate
POST /api/v1/rollouts/{id}/actions - {promote, pause, abort, resume} with reason + audit metadata
GET /api/v1/rollouts/{id}/status - returns traffic, healthSignals, rollbackState, history
sdk_helpers: createRollout(params, {idempotencyKey}) -> {rolloutId} - validates args client-side and retries safely using idempotencyKey
updateTraffic(rolloutId, weights, {expectedVersion, idempotencyKey}) - optimistic concurrency with server-side version checks
observeHealth(rolloutId, {window, signals}) -> healthSummary - wrapper that returns normalized signals (latency, error_rate, custom_eval)
reconcileLocalState(rolloutId, localDesired) - helper to align local SDK intent with control-plane state and expose diff for operator review
withRolloutGuard(fn, opts) - higher-order helper to run sensitive write operations with pre-checks, permission assertions, and rollback on failure
permission_scopes: rollout:view - read-only access to rollout metadata/status
rollout:update - modify traffic/strategy (can be scoped to project/route)
rollout:promote - one-click promote baseline->target (entails increased risk)
rollout:abort - force abort and immediate traffic failback
idempotency_model: Clients MUST supply an idempotency_key for create/update API calls that mutate rollout state. Server returns 409 if conflicting expectedVersion provided. Server keeps a 7-day idempotency cache for mutating operations; SDK will surface a clear retry/duplicate error. Idempotency semantics are at the rollout action level (createTrafficChange, toggleShadow).
consistency_and_concurrency: Adopt optimistic concurrency for traffic updates (expectedVersion). We accept eventual consistency between control-plane and edge routing for up to 30s in typical regions; document staleness windows and expose per-region last-applied timestamps in status. Trade-off: stronger linearizability would increase runtime latency and complexity for Dedicated/Private deployments; prefer eventual consistency with strong audit trail for iteration 1.
acceptance_criteria: API endpoints accept and validate rollout strategies and persist audit metadata
SDK exposes create/update helpers with idempotency and optimistic concurrency primitives
Console shows rollout timeline, current traffic split, and a one-click abort/promote control
Auto-rollback triggers when health signals cross configured thresholds and emits a rollout:aborted audit event
Permission checks enforce scopes and operations appear in audit logs with actor and reason
test_plan: Unit tests for SDK helpers: idempotency retry, expectedVersion rejection, and reconcile diff behavior
Integration tests: end-to-end create -> ramp -> rollback using a local mock runtime; assert traffic and audit events
Chaos tests: simulate region outage and ensure graceful fallback to baseline in <120s for canary with abort enabled
Load tests: concurrent traffic updates (100 clients) to validate optimistic concurrency and idempotency cache behavior
Security review: scope enforcement tests and audit log tamper-resistance checks
updates: 2026-02-22 - Kickoff: Aligned with ENG and Console teams. Agreed on optimistic concurrency and idempotency cache window (7 days).
2026-02-28 - Design review: Console team requested a lightweight timeline UI; added GET /api/v1/rollouts/{id}/status to expose history. Assigned ENG-19044 for control-plane persistence schema.
2026-03-04 - Legal & Compliance: Confirmed audit metadata retention for Dedicated/Private deployments must be configurable. Marked security_review_required=true.
2026-03-10 - Alpha plan: SDK TS prototype to be delivered in Cycle 2026-W10; integration harness ticket created (ENG-19101).
risks: Misconfigured auto-rollback could cause unnecessary aborts for noisy signals; mitigated by cooldown windows and manual override
Idempotency cache growth for high-frequency CI-driven rollouts; will monitor and impose quota/eviction policy
Permission model complexity when mapping org roles to rollout scopes in Private deployments; may require follow-up RBAC work
